Among the rising peaks of the Sol’Kesh highlands, a single chirp pierces the calm morning air. For the blister grubs tunneling beneath 
the stone cliffs, this chirp is a deafening explosion of sound, shattering the cliff face in minute craters and exposing the crushed grubs 
for the little sparrow to snatch. Th ough small and skittish, these solitary birds have adapted their far reaching ability to communicate 
with each other over vast distances to a devastating effect when close. With a highly specialized resonating chamber within their 
crested beak, they can chirp tight bands of sound that can shatter stone and ironwood when next to the surface. While this can strain 
the delicate bones within its skull, the birds will not hesitate to use it when threatened by predators.
